newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares recoup losses, end modestly higher.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares recoup losses, end modestly higher.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended higher on Monday after trading lower for most of the session as firmer Wall Street stock prices helped boost market sentiment here, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most liquid shares closed up 0.28 percent at 9,328 points. Market turnover was 556.3 million reais ($524.8 million).
The market mood improved after Wall Street appeared to have discounted an expected U.S. interest rate rise one day before the Federal Reserve meets to decide if it's time to tighten the economy.
"If the Fed decides to raise rates 25 basis points as most analysts predict, the impact will now be less strong," a senior trader said.
Bellwether Telebras preferred ended up 0.68 percent at 113.70 reais, while its common stock rose 1.1 percent to 110.40 reais after banks reiterated their buy ratings on the voting shares.
State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce preferred lost 1.39 percent to 24.85 reais.
State oil firm Petrobras preferred fell 1.81 percent, closing at 217 reais.
The Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index .IEE, comprising the nine most active shares in the electrical sector, fell 0.71 percent to close at 2,527 points.
Analysts said the local bolsa could open up, still reflecting Wall Street's rebound, but cautiously as investors await the outcome of the Fed meeting.
